title: The Elves and the Shoemaker
blurb: Someone finishes the shoemaker's work each night. Nobody knows who.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… there was a shoemaker who was very poor. He worked hard, and he was honest, [sad] but things had gone badly for him, and at last he had only enough leather left in the whole shop to make one single pair of shoes.

[softly] So that evening he cut the leather out, ready to sew in the morning. [gently] Then he said his prayers, and he went to bed.

[surprised] In the morning, he came down to his bench… [short pause] and stopped.

[excited] The shoes were finished. [curious] Not just finished — they were beautiful. Every stitch was small and straight and perfect. He turned them over in his hands and could not find one single fault.

[thoughtful] He put them in the window. [happy] And before the morning was out, a customer paid so well for them that he could buy leather for TWO pairs.

[calmly] That night he cut out both pairs, and left them on the bench, and went to bed.

[surprised] And in the morning — there they were. Both pairs. Finished. Perfect.

[excited] And so it went on. Whatever he cut out at night was made up by morning. [happy] Soon he had good custom, and money in the box, and food on the table, and he was not poor any more.

[curious] Now one evening, not long before Christmas, the shoemaker said to his wife, [thoughtful] “What if we sat up tonight, and saw who it is that helps us so?”

[excited] His wife thought that was a very good idea. [whispers] So they lit one small candle, and they hid themselves behind the coats that hung in the corner… and they waited.

[softly] The clock struck eleven. [short pause] Nothing.

[whispers] The clock struck twelve. [surprised] And in through the door came two little men. Two tiny naked little men, with nothing on at all.

[excited] They hopped up onto the bench, took up the leather, and began to work. [amused] Their little fingers went so fast that the shoemaker could hardly follow them — stitching, hammering, tapping — [playfully] until every shoe was done. And then they ran away.

[warmly] The next morning the wife said, “Those little men have made us rich. I should like to do something for them. [sad] Did you see? They had nothing to wear, and they must be so cold.”

[excited] So she sewed them each a little shirt, and a coat, and a waistcoat, and a pair of trousers. [playfully] And the shoemaker made two tiny pairs of shoes.

[whispers] That night they laid the little clothes out on the bench instead of leather. [short pause] And they hid, and they watched.

[surprised] At midnight the elves came in — and stopped. [excited] They picked up the little shirts. They pulled on the little trousers. And then they jumped, and they danced, and they skipped all round the room for joy.

[warmly] And they danced right out of the door. They never came back again. [softly] But everything went well for that shoemaker for the rest of his life.
